items.description: app/routes/ contains no import of the ORM session or any SQLAlchemy Session object (boundary layering contract)
app/services/ contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM symbol (Session, declarative_base, Column, etc.) — ORM-only contract
No hardcoded database connection string appears in any app/ source file; the connection is read exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable
app/routes/ contains no server-side HTML template rendering call; every route handler returns a JSON response (NFR-F1-5 boundary-returns-JSON)
Filing a stock record via the API endpoint durably persists the submitted SKU, location, quantity, and combined inventory_code so the record is readable immediately after the write
Attempting to insert a stock_records row with a NULL quantity, sku, location, or inventory_code against the real-branch DB raises a NOT NULL constraint violation
Retrieving a previously filed stock record via the API returns the exact quantity and combined inventory_code that were submitted at file time
When a required field is omitted from a file-stock request the error payload names that specific field rather than returning a generic message (NFR-F1-6 field-specific validation)
Filing stock a second time for the same SKU-and-location pair results in exactly one record for that pair rather than a duplicate
Filing stock a second time for the same SKU-and-location pair returns a success response with no error surfaced to the caller
Filing two records with the same per-run-unique (sku, location) pair against the real-branch DB results in exactly one row in stock_records (unique constraint PI1 enforced)
A concurrent duplicate-key write for the same (sku, location) pair completes with exactly one row stored against the real-branch DB — the upsert runs in a single transaction (PI4 atomicity)
After an in-place upsert on an existing (sku, location) row the created_at value in the real-branch DB is identical to the value recorded at first insert (audit-immutability NFR-F1-1)
The service layer rejects a file-stock write whose quantity is negative before any DB interaction occurs, with no negative row stored against the real-branch DB (NFR-F1-2 service-layer guard)
Attempting to persist a stock_records row with quantity -1 directly against the real-branch DB raises the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint violation
The Alembic migration for stock_records can be downgraded one step and then upgraded again against the real-branch DB without error (PI5 migration reversibility)
Rows seeded with per-run-unique keys before the stock_records migration is applied are present with their original field values after the upgrade completes (PI5 data-preservation)
